name: Infective dermatitis associated with HTLV-1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: La Grenade et al. diagnostic criteria for infective dermatitis associated with HTLV-1

criteria.description: Chronic, severe, exudative dermatitis involving scalp, axillae, groin, and retroauricular areas
Presence of Staphylococcus aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes superinfection
Chronic relapsing course of dermatitis with partial response to antibiotics

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic exudative dermatitis in typical distribution, HTLV-1 seropositivity, and bacterial superinfection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by serology; skin biopsy is not diagnostic but may exclude other dermatoses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic exudative eczematous dermatitis of scalp and retroauricular areas
searchTerms: chronic scaly rash on scalp and behind ears
eczema with oozing on scalp and retroauricular area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic exudative dermatitis of axillae and groin
searchTerms: long-lasting rash in armpits and groin
chronic moist dermatitis in skin folds
exudative skin inflammation in axilla and groin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent bacterial superinfection with Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes
pathognomonic.notes: Leads to crusting and oozing lesions
searchTerms: staph or strep skin infections recurring

common.symptomName: Dry, scaly skin in affected areas

rare.symptomName: Neurological manifestations including HAM/TSP (HTLV-1 associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis)

laboratory: Positive HTLV-1 serology (ELISA and confirmatory Western blot or PCR)
Bacterial culture positive for Staphylococcus aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes from skin lesions
imaging: MRI may be indicated if neurological symptoms develop to assess for HAM/TSP
genetic: HTLV-1 proviral DNA integration detected by PCR
other: Skin biopsy shows spongiotic dermatitis with secondary bacterial colonization but is nonspecific

distinguishingFeatures: Typically involves seborrheic areas without bacterial superinfection
Localized bacterial infection without chronic relapsing dermatitis

redFlags: Development of neurological symptoms suggestive of HAM/TSP
Rapidly spreading cellulitis or systemic infection
Failure to respond to appropriate antibiotic therapy
references: La Grenade L, et al. Infective dermatitis associated with HTLV-1: clinical and immunological features. Lancet. 1998.
Gessain A, Cassar O. Epidemiological Aspects and World Distribution of HTLV-1 Infection. Front Microbiol. 2012.
Proietti FA, et al. Global epidemiology of HTLV-1 infection and associated diseases. Oncogene. 2005.
